title: Emotions (moods)
description: Emotions a client names and rates for intensity (0 to 100) in thought records and in the emotions slot of formulation models, grouped into families, with valence (positive or negative hedonic tone). Code single feeling words here; words such as worthless, useless or a failure are thoughts or beliefs and belong in thought or belief schemes, not here. Positive emotions support activity monitoring and protective factors.
sources: Greenberger-Padesky-2016 § Ch. 4 Identifying and Rating Moods
Beck-2021 § Ch. 13 Emotions
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions
Fredrickson-2001 § The Broaden-and-Build Theory of Positive Emotions

concepts.label: Anxious
concepts.definition: Tense, uneasy apprehension about a possible future threat or uncertain outcome; anticipatory and often diffuse rather than tied to present danger.
concepts.client_wording: Nervous or uneasy, expecting that something bad might happen.
concepts.example: The night before a job interview: "I'll freeze and they'll think I'm useless." Anxious 70.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Anxiety Disorders introduction (fear versus anxiety)
Clark-Beck-2010 § Ch. 1 Anxiety: A Common but Multifaceted Condition
Greenberger-Padesky-2016 § Ch. 14 Understanding Your Anxiety

concepts.label: Afraid
concepts.definition: Alarm in response to a threat perceived as present or imminent, preparing the body to fight, flee or freeze.
concepts.client_wording: Scared, as if the danger is right here, right now.
concepts.example: A dog runs toward me barking. Afraid 90.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Anxiety Disorders introduction (fear versus anxiety)
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Panicky
concepts.definition: Abrupt surge of intense fear peaking within minutes, usually with strong bodily sensations and fears of dying, collapsing or losing control.
concepts.client_wording: A sudden rush of terror, often with a racing heart and a sense that something awful is happening.
concepts.example: In the supermarket queue: "I'm having a heart attack." Panicky 95.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Panic Attack Specifier
Clark-1986 § The cognitive model of panic

concepts.label: Dread
concepts.definition: Heavy, anticipatory fear of a specific upcoming event that feels unavoidable and bad.
concepts.client_wording: A heavy sense that something bad is coming and I can't stop it.
concepts.example: All Sunday evening before Monday's meeting with my manager. Dread 80.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions
Clark-Beck-2010 § Ch. 1 Anxiety: A Common but Multifaceted Condition

concepts.label: Overwhelmed
concepts.definition: Sense that demands or emotions exceed one's resources to cope, often with agitation, paralysis or shutting down.
concepts.client_wording: Too much at once, more than I can handle.
concepts.example: Opening 40 unread emails on my first day back after sick leave. Overwhelmed 85.
sources: Lazarus-Folkman-1984 § Ch. 2 Cognitive Appraisal Processes
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Suspicious
concepts.definition: Wary, fearful expectation that others intend harm, deceit or ridicule; common in paranoia, after trauma and in jealousy.
concepts.client_wording: On guard, as if people might be against me or up to something.
concepts.example: Two coworkers stop talking as I walk in: "They're plotting against me." Suspicious 70.
sources: Freeman-2007 § The paranoia continuum
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Sad
concepts.definition: Painful feeling of loss, disappointment or unmet need, usually linked to a specific event and easing with time.
concepts.client_wording: Down, low or unhappy about something.
concepts.example: After my closest friend moved to another state. Sad 60.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions
Greenberger-Padesky-2016 § Ch. 4 Identifying and Rating Moods

concepts.label: Depressed
concepts.definition: Persistent, pervasive low mood across most of the day and many situations, often with low energy and loss of interest.
concepts.client_wording: Low and heavy most of the time, not just about one thing.
concepts.example: Low most days for a month, even on my birthday. Depressed 80.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Major Depressive Disorder
Greenberger-Padesky-2016 § Ch. 13 Understanding Your Depression

concepts.label: Grief
concepts.definition: Sorrow and yearning after losing a loved person or something deeply valued; comes in waves. Prolonged, impairing grief warrants assessment.
concepts.client_wording: Deep sorrow and missing someone or something I have lost.
concepts.example: Finding Mom's handwriting on an old birthday card. Grief 90.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Prolonged Grief Disorder
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Disappointed
concepts.definition: Sadness when an outcome falls short of one's hopes or expectations of oneself, others or events.
concepts.client_wording: Let down because things did not turn out how I hoped.
concepts.example: My exam grade came back lower than I expected. Disappointed 50.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Angry
concepts.definition: Activated feeling in response to a perceived wrong, unfairness, threat or blocked goal, preparing a person to confront or defend.
concepts.client_wording: Mad or furious, like something is unfair or wrong.
concepts.example: My partner made weekend plans without asking me: "They don't respect me." Angry 75.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions
Deffenbacher-2011 § Conceptualization of anger
Greenberger-Padesky-2016 § Ch. 15 Understanding Your Anger, Guilt, and Shame

concepts.label: Irritated
concepts.definition: Low-level, easily triggered anger or impatience; persistent irritability is common in depression, anxiety, mania and poor sleep.
concepts.client_wording: Annoyed, snappy or short-tempered over small things.
concepts.example: The sound of my partner chewing at dinner. Irritated 40.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions
APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Generalized Anxiety Disorder (irritability criterion)

concepts.label: Frustrated
concepts.definition: Anger-related feeling when effort is blocked or progress toward a goal is repeatedly thwarted.
concepts.client_wording: Fed up because I keep trying and getting nowhere.
concepts.example: The online form crashed for the third time. Frustrated 65.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Resentful
concepts.definition: Lingering, simmering anger about a past or ongoing perceived injustice, often unexpressed and kept alive by going over it.
concepts.client_wording: Bitter about being treated unfairly, and I can't let it go.
concepts.example: Every time my brother mentions the inheritance. Resentful 70.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Ashamed
concepts.definition: Painful sense that the whole self is bad, defective or inferior, with urges to hide, withdraw or disappear.
concepts.client_wording: Feeling bad about who I am and wanting to hide.
concepts.example: After crying in front of my team: "I'm pathetic." Ashamed 85.
sources: Tangney-etal-1996 § General discussion
Gilbert-2009 § Shame and self-criticism
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions
Greenberger-Padesky-2016 § Ch. 15 Understanding Your Anger, Guilt, and Shame

concepts.label: Embarrassed
concepts.definition: Brief, lighter discomfort after a public social slip or unwanted attention; less about the core self than shame.
concepts.client_wording: Awkward and self-conscious after something goes wrong in front of others.
concepts.example: I called my teacher "Mom" in front of the class. Embarrassed 55.
sources: Tangney-etal-1996 § General discussion
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Humiliated
concepts.definition: Intense shame from being degraded, mocked or exposed by others, often in public, frequently with anger at those responsible.
concepts.client_wording: Put down or made to feel small by someone, often in front of others.
concepts.example: My boss mocked my report in the team meeting. Humiliated 90.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Guilty
concepts.definition: Distress about a specific action or omission judged to have caused harm or broken one's own standards, with urges to repair.
concepts.client_wording: Feeling I did something wrong and wanting to put it right.
concepts.example: "I snapped at my son and made him cry." Guilty 70.
sources: Tangney-etal-1996 § General discussion
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions
Greenberger-Padesky-2016 § Ch. 15 Understanding Your Anger, Guilt, and Shame

concepts.label: Regretful
concepts.definition: Sorrow over a past choice or missed chance, wishing it had gone differently, with or without any moral wrongdoing.
concepts.client_wording: Wishing I had done things differently.
concepts.example: "If only I'd taken that job offer." Regretful 60.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Disgusted
concepts.definition: Revulsion toward something seen as contaminating, offensive or morally violating, with urges to expel, avoid or wash.
concepts.client_wording: Revolted or grossed out, wanting to get away from it.
concepts.example: Touching the door handle of a public restroom. Disgusted 80.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions
Rachman-2004 § Fear and disgust

concepts.label: Self-disgust
concepts.definition: Disgust directed at one's own body, actions or whole self; associated with later depressive symptoms.
concepts.client_wording: Revolted by myself or my body.
concepts.example: Catching my reflection after a binge: "I'm repulsive." Self-disgust 75.
sources: Powell-etal-2013 § Discussion
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Feeling dirty (mental contamination)
concepts.definition: Sense of internal dirtiness or pollution arising without physical contact, often after violation, betrayal or unwanted thoughts; drives washing.
concepts.client_wording: Feeling dirty or unclean inside, even though I haven't touched anything.
concepts.example: The memory of the assault came back and I needed to shower. Feeling dirty 85.
sources: Rachman-2004 § Mental pollution
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Hurt
concepts.definition: Emotional pain from perceiving that someone important does not value the relationship as much as one wants.
concepts.client_wording: Wounded by something someone close said or did.
concepts.example: My sister forgot my birthday. Hurt 70.
sources: Leary-etal-1998 § Causes of hurt feelings
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Rejected
concepts.definition: Hurt from being excluded, turned down or pushed away by others; may activate fears of being unlovable.
concepts.client_wording: Unwanted or left out by people I care about.
concepts.example: Seeing photos of a party I wasn't invited to. Rejected 80.
sources: Leary-etal-1998 § Causes of hurt feelings
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Betrayed
alt_labels: let down by someone I trusted
concepts.definition: Hurt and anger when a trusted person breaks trust, a promise or loyalty.
concepts.client_wording: Someone I trusted broke that trust.
concepts.example: Finding out my friend shared my secret. Betrayed 90.
sources: Leary-etal-1998 § Causes of hurt feelings

concepts.label: Lonely
concepts.definition: Distress at a gap between wanted and actual social connection, in quantity or quality; can occur when surrounded by people.
concepts.client_wording: Alone or cut off, even when people are around.
concepts.example: Eating dinner alone again on a Friday night. Lonely 75.
sources: Hawkley-Cacioppo-2010 § Definition of loneliness
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Longing
concepts.definition: Aching wish for an absent person, place or time that is not lost for good, as in separation or homesickness.
concepts.client_wording: Missing someone or somewhere so much it aches.
concepts.example: Holidays far from my family back home. Longing 70.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Jealous
concepts.definition: Fear and anger about losing a valued relationship, or a person's attention, to a rival; involves three people.
concepts.client_wording: Afraid someone will take away a person who matters to me.
concepts.example: My partner laughs at a coworker's message: "They'd rather be with them." Jealous 80.
sources: Parrott-Smith-1993 § Introduction
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Envious
concepts.definition: Painful wish for another person's advantage, success or possession, often with resentment or inferiority; involves two people.
concepts.client_wording: Wanting what someone else has, and feeling worse because they have it.
concepts.example: Scrolling past a friend's promotion announcement. Envious 60.
sources: Parrott-Smith-1993 § Introduction
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Hopeless
concepts.definition: Expectation that the future is bleak and nothing will improve; a key suicide risk marker that always prompts risk assessment.
concepts.client_wording: Like nothing will ever get better.
concepts.example: "There's no point trying, it'll always be like this." Hopeless 90.
sources: Beck-etal-1974 § Introduction
APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Major Depressive Disorder (suicide risk)

concepts.label: Helpless
concepts.definition: Feeling that one's actions cannot influence important outcomes.
concepts.client_wording: Powerless, like nothing I do makes a difference.
concepts.example: Watching my father's illness get worse. Helpless 85.
sources: Abramson-etal-1978 § Introduction

concepts.label: Defeated
concepts.definition: Sense of having lost a struggle for valued goals, status or self-worth, with a pull to give up.
concepts.client_wording: Beaten down, like I've lost and there's no fight left.
concepts.example: Rejected for the tenth job in a row. Defeated 80.
sources: Gilbert-Allan-1998 § Introduction
OConnor-Kirtley-2018 § Motivational phase

concepts.label: Trapped
concepts.definition: Strong wish to escape a painful situation or inner state combined with sensing no way out; central to suicide risk models.
concepts.client_wording: Stuck in how things are, with no way out.
concepts.example: "I can't leave this marriage and I can't stand staying." Trapped 90.
sources: Gilbert-Allan-1998 § Introduction
OConnor-Kirtley-2018 § Motivational phase

concepts.label: Discouraged
concepts.definition: Loss of confidence and motivation after setbacks; milder and more situation-bound than hopelessness.
concepts.client_wording: Losing heart after things keep going wrong.
concepts.example: Third week of therapy and still low: "This isn't working." Discouraged 55.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Numb
concepts.definition: Reduced capacity to feel emotions, especially positive or loving ones; common after trauma and in depression.
concepts.client_wording: Can't feel much of anything, as if my feelings are switched off.
concepts.example: At my friend's wedding I felt nothing at all. Numb 80.
sources: Litz-Gray-2002 § Model of posttraumatic emotional functioning
APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (inability to experience positive emotions)

concepts.label: Empty
concepts.definition: Chronic sense of inner hollowness or lack of substance, distinct from sadness; a feature of borderline personality disorder and depression.
concepts.client_wording: Hollow inside, like something important is missing.
concepts.example: Home alone after work, scrolling with no sense of who I am. Empty 75.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Borderline Personality Disorder (chronic emptiness)
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Unable to enjoy (anhedonia)
concepts.definition: Markedly reduced interest in, or pleasure from, activities once enjoyed; a core symptom of depression.
concepts.client_wording: Nothing feels enjoyable or interesting anymore.
concepts.example: I went fishing, which I used to love, and felt nothing. Enjoyment 0.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Major Depressive Disorder
Beck-2021 § Ch. 7 Activity Scheduling

concepts.label: Bored
concepts.definition: Aversive state of wanting, but being unable, to engage attention in satisfying activity.
concepts.client_wording: Restless and fed up because nothing holds my attention.
concepts.example: A long empty Sunday with nothing planned: "A drink would help." Bored 70.
sources: Eastwood-etal-2012 § Defining boredom
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Happy
concepts.definition: Pleasant feeling of joy, gladness or satisfaction when things go well or valued needs are met.
concepts.client_wording: Glad, cheerful or joyful.
concepts.example: My daughter called with good news. Happy 70.
sources: Fredrickson-2001 § The Broaden-and-Build Theory of Positive Emotions
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions
Greenberger-Padesky-2016 § Ch. 16 Maintaining Your Gains and Experiencing More Happiness

concepts.label: Enjoyment (pleasure)
concepts.definition: Pleasure taken in an activity itself; recorded as the pleasure rating in activity monitoring and scheduling.
concepts.client_wording: How much I liked doing something.
concepts.example: Walk in the park with the dog: pleasure rated high, even though I was tired.
sources: Beck-2021 § Ch. 7 Activity Scheduling

concepts.label: Sense of achievement (mastery)
concepts.definition: Satisfaction from completing a task or meeting a challenge, judged against current ability; recorded as the achievement or mastery rating.
concepts.client_wording: Feeling I got something done or handled something hard.
concepts.example: On a low day I paid one overdue bill: achievement rated high.
sources: Beck-2021 § Ch. 7 Activity Scheduling

concepts.label: Proud
concepts.definition: Pleasant self-evaluation after an achievement or after acting in line with one's values.
concepts.client_wording: Pleased with myself for something I did.
concepts.example: I spoke up in the meeting even though I was nervous. Proud 65.
sources: Fredrickson-2001 § The Broaden-and-Build Theory of Positive Emotions
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Calm
concepts.definition: Low-arousal state of physical and mental ease; the target state of relaxation and arousal-reduction techniques.
concepts.client_wording: Relaxed and settled in body and mind.
concepts.example: After ten minutes of slow breathing on the porch. Calm 60.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions
Gilbert-2009 § Three types of affect regulation system

concepts.label: Soothed (safe and comforted)
concepts.definition: Felt safeness and warmth from care or self-compassion, linked to the soothing affect system in compassion-focused therapy.
concepts.client_wording: Comforted and safe, like someone, or I, am looking after me.
concepts.example: Putting a hand on my chest and speaking kindly to myself after a mistake. Soothed 50.
sources: Gilbert-2009 § Three types of affect regulation system

concepts.label: Hopeful
concepts.definition: Expectation that valued goals are reachable and things can improve, with a sense of pathways to get there; protective against despair.
concepts.client_wording: Things could get better, and I can help make that happen.
concepts.example: After making a plan with my therapist: "This might actually help." Hopeful 55.
sources: Snyder-2002 § Hope theory
Beck-etal-1974 § Introduction

concepts.label: Confident
concepts.definition: Expectation that one can carry out a task or handle a situation successfully (self-efficacy).
concepts.client_wording: Sure that I can handle this.
concepts.example: Before my third practice presentation. Confident 70.
sources: Bandura-1977 § Efficacy expectations

concepts.label: Interested
concepts.definition: Engaged curiosity that draws a person toward exploring and learning; the opposite pull to boredom and withdrawal.
concepts.client_wording: Curious and drawn in by something.
concepts.example: Lost track of time reading about bird migration. Interested 70.
sources: Fredrickson-2001 § The Broaden-and-Build Theory of Positive Emotions
Watson-etal-1988 § Method

concepts.label: Connected (loved and close)
concepts.definition: Warmth and closeness with others, including love and a sense of belonging; the counterpart of loneliness.
concepts.client_wording: Close to people, cared about and belonging.
concepts.example: Cooking dinner with my sister and laughing. Connected 80.
sources: Fredrickson-2001 § The Broaden-and-Build Theory of Positive Emotions
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions
Hawkley-Cacioppo-2010 § Definition of loneliness

concepts.label: Relieved
concepts.definition: Drop in distress when a feared outcome passes or is escaped; relief after avoidance or a safety behavior can keep fear going.
concepts.client_wording: The weight lifting when something I feared is over or avoided.
concepts.example: I cancelled the party at the last minute. Relieved 80, and the next invite felt even harder.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions
Clark-1986 § The cognitive model of panic

concepts.label: Elated
concepts.definition: Intense, expansive happiness; when persistent, out of proportion or with reduced need for sleep, assess for hypomania or mania.
concepts.client_wording: Extremely high or on top of the world, more than usual for me.
concepts.example: Three nights of little sleep, full of plans: "I can do anything." Elated 95.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Bipolar I Disorder (manic episode)
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Yearning (for someone who died)
alt_labels: aching for the person who died
concepts.definition: Intense, persistent longing for a person who has died; a core symptom of prolonged grief when it stays daily and impairing.
concepts.client_wording: Aching to have the person who died back, again and again.
concepts.example: Hearing his favorite song in a shop. Yearning 85.
sources: Prigerson-etal-2021 § Prolonged grief disorder criteria
Shear-2015 § Clinical features
